findings.title: Unsubscribe route has no matching Ember template
findings.body: The route is declared as top-level `topicUnsubscribe`, but the template was added at `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which is the path for a nested `topic.unsubscribe` route. A top-level `topicUnsubscribe` route looks for `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs`. The route defines no `renderTemplate`, so the client-side unsubscribe page will fail to render or error. Either nest the route inside the existing `topic` resource as `this.route('unsubscribe', ...)`, or move the template to `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs`.

findings.title: unsubscribe action crashes when TopicUser record is missing
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by` can return nil when the logged-in user has no TopicUser record for this topic. Any logged-in user can open `/t/:id/unsubscribe` for a visible topic they have never interacted with; the action is not restricted to users coming from an email. On line 107 it immediately calls `tu.notification_level`, so a missing record raises `NoMethodError` and returns 500. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)` or otherwise initialize/handle a missing record.

findings.title: Per-topic unsubscribe mutates state via GET without CSRF or token
findings.body: The new unsubscribe routes are GET and `TopicsController#unsubscribe` mutates the user's `TopicUser#notification_level` on each request. Rails CSRF protection does not cover GET, and the URL contains no per-recipient token. A logged-in user who can be induced to load `https://.../t/123/unsubscribe` (for example through an image on an attacker-controlled page) will have their topic notification setting changed without intent. The same issue means email scanners/prefetchers that carry a session cookie could trigger it. This should be a POST with CSRF protection, or use a non-mutating tokenized flow.

findings.title: Unsubscribe does not stop all topic notifications for watching/tracking users
findings.body: When `notification_level` is `watching` or `tracking`, this action lowers it to `regular`. The link text promises to stop receiving notifications about the topic, but `regular` still permits reply and mention notifications for that topic, which are exactly some of the notification emails this link is attached to. A watching/tracking user can click the unsubscribe link and still continue receiving other notifications for the same topic. To honor the advertised behavior, the action should set `muted` (or explicitly use a different, clearly communicated level).
